limits: Age adaptation and tactical alternatives await coaching review. Static setup: no skating speed, interception timing or uniquely optimal route has been validated. Positional references are examples, not scored targets.

questions.prompt: Which Navy player is assigned the first wall contest?

options.text: C
D1
F1

questions.explanation: F1 is identified in the wall contest; YOU have the second-player role.

questions.prompt: Choose two things that can make second support useful.

options.text: A read of the next loose touch
Separation from the first contest
Standing on F1’s position to add another label

questions.explanation: A second role should complement the first player and the outlet, not merely duplicate them.

questions.prompt: Order one second-support read.

options.text: Watch the contest and puck direction
Check C and the opposing support
Move to the next useful touch or containment position

questions.explanation: The direction of the next touch determines the action; the static puck does not predict the winner.

questions.prompt: Move YOU closer to Navy’s net than the battle to illustrate a second-touch support pocket.
questions.explanation: This reference separates YOU from F1 and leaves a possible connection to C. Different bounces require different positions.

questions.prompt: Gold 2 moves onto C’s outlet. Which two checks help you adjust?

options.text: Look for the next available pass if Navy wins the puck
Recheck whether C can still receive safely
Assume F1 has won the puck because Gold 2 moved

questions.explanation: Winning the battle does not guarantee the originally planned outlet.

questions.prompt: Explain a useful second-player job if F1 does not win the puck cleanly.
questions.explanation: Contain an exit, collect a loose touch or support defensive recovery; tie the answer to Gold 1, Gold 2 and C.

title: Protect possession while a teammate changes
objective: Make a conditional puck-management choice during a stated substitution.
briefing: F3 is changing at the bench and is unavailable for the next few moments. YOU hold the puck in the neutral zone. D2 is behind YOU; F1 and F2 are farther ahead. This is a possession exercise, not a too-many-players rules test. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: The briefing states F3 is unavailable; the scenario does not draw or count a player entering the ice.

limits: Age adaptation and tactical alternatives await coaching review. Static setup: no skating speed, interception timing or uniquely optimal route has been validated. Positional references are examples, not scored targets.

questions.prompt: Who is explicitly unavailable during this moment?

options.text: F1 up ice
F3 at the bench change
D2 behind YOU

questions.explanation: The briefing states F3 is unavailable; the scenario does not draw or count a player entering the ice.

questions.prompt: Which two checks matter while support is reduced?

options.text: The pressure from Gold 1
A belief that every change requires a blind dump
Whether D2 offers a controlled reset

questions.explanation: Possession, pressure and available support shape the choice; there is no automatic action attached to a change.

questions.prompt: Arrange one read during this change.

options.text: Confirm available teammates
Assess pressure and controlled options
Choose a play and communicate the next support need

questions.explanation: This is a stated game-management situation, not a substitution-rule sequence.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a position preserving a connection to D2.
questions.explanation: A modest retreat may maintain a reset while support changes. A forward option may still be preferable if clearly available.

questions.prompt: The new F3 arrives in a clear middle lane. What can you reconsider?

options.text: The idea that support remains reduced forever
A requirement to use D2 despite the new option
Whether a new forward connection has appeared

questions.explanation: The availability change should update the picture instead of locking in the earlier conservative plan.

questions.prompt: Why is “a teammate is changing” not enough information to demand a dump-in?
questions.explanation: Explain how pressure, control and other teammates could support a carry, pass or reset.

title: Keep an attack alive when the slot is crowded
objective: Compare a covered slot play with a low-zone support option.
briefing: YOU control at the puck-side half wall. Gold 1 shades the slot route to F2, while F1 is available below the goal line. D1 holds the high point. The exercise invites a possession read rather than requiring a shot. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: F1 is behind Gold’s goal line; D1 remains high near the blue line.

sources.use: Supports age/topic placement only. The setup, alternatives and suggested answers are original experimental coaching synthesis, not source-certified.

limits: Age adaptation and tactical alternatives await coaching review. Static setup: no skating speed, interception timing or uniquely optimal route has been validated. Positional references are examples, not scored targets.

questions.prompt: Which teammate is below the attacking goal-line area?

options.text: F1
D1
Gold 3

questions.explanation: F1 is behind Gold’s goal line; D1 remains high near the blue line.

questions.prompt: Choose two checks before using low support.

options.text: The assumption that a covered slot must still be forced
Whether the low route remains open
Whether F1 can receive away from Gold 2

questions.explanation: Low support may preserve possession, but it creates another read rather than a guaranteed scoring chance.

questions.prompt: Arrange a possession reset decision.

options.text: Recognize the crowded slot route
Compare low and high outlets
Use an available connection and reoffer

questions.explanation: A shot or carry remains possible if the picture changes; this routine does not ban them.

questions.prompt: Move YOU off the puck-side half wall to compare a new low-support angle.
questions.explanation: The example changes the relation to Gold 1 and F1. Other pockets may preserve possession better under live pressure.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 leaves the slot route to pressure YOU on the wall. What should be checked?

options.text: Only the low pass from the old picture
Whether F2’s route has become usable
The assumption that the slot is still covered identically

questions.explanation: A defender leaving one responsibility can open another, but Gold 2 may still affect the pass.

questions.prompt: Name two support areas in this scene and explain the different choices they offer.
questions.explanation: Contrast below the goal line with the high point or slot. Describe the pressure, not merely the geography.
